key_catalyst: Microsoft's CFO dismissing the AI overcapacity narrative and cutting calendar 2026 capex to ~$175B from ~$190B, with the stock soaring — the first explicit rebuttal to the AI-spending-doubt leg.
reasoning: Two of the legs memory carried as unresolved actually RESOLVED inside 9:30-15:45: Microsoft's CFO explicitly dismissed the AI-overcapacity narrative and lowered calendar 2026 capex to about $175B from roughly $190B — the first hard rebuttal after four consecutive sessions of unrebutted AI-spending doubt — while Q2 GDP and June PCE printed resilient consumer demand with easing inflation and hike fear receding, retiring the ~30% Fed-hike tail that was live two sessions ago. QQQ's +1.30% from the open is the largest intraday gain in the entire memory window and it is proportionate to that improvement, not a flat/complacent tape absorbing bad news, which is the exact configuration that made the SELLs on T-2 (+0.53%) and T-3 wrong. What remains unresolved into the close is Iran threatening a response to the latest US strikes with Brent only +1.5% to $92.10, and a 2.6% yen jump with Japan intervention talk that reprices the carry leg in Asia hours — both real overnight channels, but neither is a dated trigger and neither is the documented supply print memory set as the geopolitical SELL bar.
